emir.trade-reports.name: emir.trade-reports
emir.trade-reports.description: EMIR trade reports (one record per report submission, append-only). Both-sided reporting: each economic trade normally appears twice, once per reporting counterparty.
emir.trade-reports.application_context: Lenses SQL: query as `emir.trade-reports`. To count economic trades, COUNT(DISTINCT uti). counterparty_1 / counterparty_2 are LEIs of the legal parties -- do not join them to clearing_member_id (member codes, different concept).
emir.trade-reports.business_context: EMIR Refit reporting to a trade repository. Dual-sided: naive COUNT(*) of reports is ~2x the number of economic trades.

columns.name: uti
columns.description: Unique Transaction Identifier shared by both sides of the trade
application_rules: COUNT(DISTINCT uti) = number of economic trades; COUNT(*) counts report submissions (approx. double).

columns.name: counterparty_1
columns.description: LEI of the reporting counterparty (EMIR field 1.4) -- the legal party submitting this report

columns.name: counterparty_2
columns.description: LEI of the other counterparty (EMIR field 1.9)

columns.name: action_type
application_rules: Live trades = latest action per UTI not in (EROR, TERM); a NEWT followed by EROR is not outstanding.

columns.name: reporting_timestamp
columns.description: Time the report was submitted to the TR

etd.clearing-events.name: etd.clearing-events
etd.clearing-events.description: Clearing system lifecycle events (C7-style): NOVATION, GIVE_UP, TAKE_UP, POSITION_NETTING, TRADE_CORRECTION. Append-only event stream keyed by clearing event id.
etd.clearing-events.business_context: Post-trade clearing at the CCP. After NOVATION the CCP becomes the counterparty to each clearing member; original bilateral link is replaced.

columns.name: clearing_member_id
columns.description: Clearing member (GCM/DCM) code affected by the event. In clearing documentation this entity is often loosely called the 'counterparty' -- it is NOT the EMIR reporting counterparty.

columns.name: event_time
columns.description: Business time the clearing event took effect

etd.executions.name: etd.executions
etd.executions.description: Exchange execution (fill) events for exchange-traded derivatives. One record per fill; a single order may produce many fills. Append-only event stream.
etd.executions.application_context: Lenses SQL: query as `etd.executions` (backticks required). Append-only: aggregations over the full stream are valid.
etd.executions.business_context: ETD trade lifecycle, pre-clearing. Quantities here are unsigned lot counts; direction is carried by `side`.

columns.name: exec_id
columns.description: Unique execution/fill identifier assigned by the exchange

columns.name: order_id
columns.description: Parent order identifier; fan-out: many fills per order
application_rules: Counting orders requires COUNT(DISTINCT order_id), never COUNT(*)

columns.name: side
columns.description: Aggressor side of this fill: BUY or SELL
application_rules: Side is the execution direction, NOT the resulting position direction. A BUY fill can reduce a short position; never infer LONG/SHORT from side.

columns.name: quantity
columns.description: Unsigned number of lots in this fill (always positive)

columns.name: executing_member
columns.description: Exchange member that executed the fill (member code)

columns.name: exec_time
columns.description: Business event time of the fill (exchange matching timestamp). Use this for trade-date logic, not Kafka _meta.timestamp (ingestion time).

etd.positions.name: etd.positions
etd.positions.description: COMPACTED state topic: current net position per key (clearing_member_id, account, contract_series). Each record is a full replacement snapshot for its key, not a delta.
etd.positions.application_context: Lenses SQL: query as `etd.positions`. COMPACTION SEMANTICS: the snapshot engine may return multiple historical records per key; aggregating (SUM/COUNT) over all records double-counts. Valid current-state reads must take the latest record per key (max _meta.offset per partition/key) before any aggregation.
etd.positions.business_context: Netted post-clearing positions maintained by the CCP.

columns.name: net_quantity
columns.description: SIGNED net lots: positive = LONG, negative = SHORT. Gross long/short cannot be recovered from this field.
application_rules: Total open interest per series = SUM(ABS(net_quantity))/2 over the LATEST record per key only.
Never SUM net_quantity across the topic history: compaction means history contains superseded snapshots.

columns.name: as_of_time
columns.description: Business time this snapshot became effective

refdata.contracts.name: refdata.contracts
refdata.contracts.description: COMPACTED reference-data topic: one current record per contract series (key = contract_series).
refdata.contracts.application_context: Lenses SQL: query as `refdata.contracts`. Compacted: use latest record per key.

columns.name: contract_series
columns.description: Contract series code (join key across topics)

columns.name: contract_multiplier
columns.description: Value of one point per contract; notional = price * multiplier * lots

counterparty.clearing_member.label: counterparty
counterparty.clearing_member.definition: A member of the CCP that clears trades (GCM/DCM). NOT a legal counterparty to the economic trade for EMIR reporting purposes; faces the CCP post-novation. The word 'counterparty' in clearing system docs (e.g. Eurex C7) usually means this entity.

counterparty.emir_reporting.label: counterparty
counterparty.emir_reporting.definition: The entity on whose behalf an EMIR trade report is submitted (EMIR RTS field 1.4). Identified by LEI. One of the two legal parties to the derivative contract.

mappings.justification: EMIR reporting counterparty is a role-restricted subset of the FIBO derivatives counterparty

position.net.label: net
position.net.definition: Post-netting exposure per (clearing member, account, contract series). Signed: positive = long, negative = short. Current state, not a flow.
